new_statements.translation: ... tones. In the present state of study of the language we can only posit the existence of three tones in Toram, namely high, marked by an acute accent, mid, not marked graphically here, and low, marked by a grave accent. Examples: kíllú 'caterpillar', gardyi 'elephant', jòorè 'warthog', kèbin 'buffalo', bóokok ...

new_statements.rule_in_words: Toram is described as a tone language with three level tones (high, mid, low) marked lexically on every syllable; the only 'accent' mentioned is the acute/grave diacritic used to write tone. The sketch's phonology section (vowels, consonants, tones) contains no statement about word stress or an intensity accent.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the author flags the three-tone analysis itself as provisional ('dans l'état actuel de l'étude.. nous ne pouvons que retenir l'existence de trois tons').
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone on citation forms of nouns/verbs in a c. 450-item wordlist (pp. 252-263); no phrase-level or stress-domain discussion. Text seen only as Google Books snippets of pp. 249-251 (verbatim, both print id unEB9cNse84C and e-book id 6AT1DwAAQBAJ); full chapter not opened.
new_statements.identity_note: Alio 2004 describes 'le toram du Salamat' (Toram/Torom of the Salamat region, Chad) = Glottolog tora1267, ISO trj; no dialect differentiation is made. Not to be confused with the 'Mubi-Toram' group label used by Jungraithmayr/Takács for the whole East Chadic B1.2 cluster.
